description: Sixteen sequences of up to 16 steps, each step holding a pitch, two gates, a tie and a slide; song mode chains sequences as a series of up to 16 phrases, 256 steps in all

params.text: Switches the keyboard back to entering note pitches
Switches the keyboard from entering pitches to entering one of the 12 advanced gate types; pressing it again alternates between setting gate 1 and gate 2
In the SEQ position the selected sequence plays and its contents can be edited; in SONG the series of phrases plays and is edited, and sequence contents cannot be changed
Selects which sequence is edited and played in SEQ mode, and which sequence the selected phrase points at in SONG mode; it also enters lengths, transpositions and rotations
Starts and stops the sequencer
Copies the selected sequence, or the part of it set by the copy-paste switch; in SONG mode it copies part of the song
Pastes what was copied. Copying in one mode and pasting in the other runs a shortcut instead, such as randomising the pitches or filling the song with rising sequence numbers
Returns the play head to the first step of the sequence, and to the first phrase of the song in SONG mode
Puts the note of the step being edited into that octave, 4 being the octave of middle C; the lit button is the octave that step currently holds
Turns the first gate of the step being edited on or off
Turns the second gate of the step being edited on or off
Turns portamento on for the step being edited, so its pitch glides from the pitch of the step before it
How long that glide takes, from nothing up to one whole clock period; the default is a tenth of a clock period
Ties the edit head to the play head so that editing follows what is playing; with it off, the edit head is placed by clicking a step
When on, writing a note advances the edit head one step to the right
One press sets the length, by the main knob or by clicking a step; a second press sets the run mode; holding it for 2 seconds sets the clock resolution in pulses per step
One press transposes the selected sequence in semitones, a second press rotates its steps left or right, with the main knob setting the amount. Rotations are not stored
The chance that a gate 1 on a marked step reaches its output, 0 to 1. One setting serves the whole module rather than one per step
Marks the step being edited so that its first gate is output only some of the time
Ties the step being edited to the pitch of the step before it, holding one note across both. The menu option Hold tied notes governs whether gate 1 stays high across the run
Sets how much a copy takes: 4 steps, 8 steps, or the whole sequence together with its length and run mode
In SEQ mode this selects that step for editing, and its light shows the edit head in red and the play head in green; in SONG mode it selects that phrase of the song

inputs.text: A rising edge above 1V stores the voltage at CV IN into the step being edited
The voltage written into the step being edited when a write is triggered; anything from -10V to 10V is stored
A rising edge above 1V returns the play head to the first step, and to the first phrase in SONG mode
Advances the sequencer one step on each rising edge
A rising edge above 1V moves the edit head one step to the left
A rising edge above 1V moves the edit head one step to the right
A rising edge above 1V starts or stops the sequencer
Selects the sequence from outside, 0-10V spread across the 16 sequences; the menu offers note voltages or a trigger that steps to the next sequence instead

outputs.text: The pitch of the step being played, 1V per octave
The first gate of the step being played, 10V when high
The second gate of the step being played, 10V when high

notes: The onboard keyboard sets the pitch of the step being edited. Right-clicking a key enters the note and moves to the next step; holding ctrl carries the gate type over too
Holding LEN / MODE for 2 seconds sets the clock resolution in pulses per step. Above 1 the advanced gate types can be entered, and the clock must be multiplied to match
with the mouse over the sequence display, a sequence number can be typed on the computer keyboard, two key presses within one second reading as a two-digit number
in song mode, with the mouse over the sequence display, the space bar moves on to the next phrase
menu: Seq CV in level — sets how the SEQ # input is read: 0-10V across the 16 sequences, the note voltages C4-D5#, or Trig-Incr, where a trigger steps to the next sequence
Hold tied notes — keeps gate 1 high across a run of tied steps; with it off only the first step of the run carries a gate
Reset on run — returns the play head to the start every time the sequencer is started
Retrigger gates on reset — holds the gate outputs low for 1ms after a reset so a trigger-sensitive target fires again; the choices are No, Yes, and Only when Run cable is unconnected
Single shot song — plays the song once instead of repeating it
AutoStep write bounded by seq length — stops a write autostepping past the last step of the sequence
AutoSeq when writing via CV inputs — moves on to the next sequence when a write runs off the end of the current one, which turns the sequencer into a long CV recorder
Portable sequence — holds Copy sequence and Paste sequence, which move the selected sequence between this module and other sequencers that support the format; it can be used in SEQ mode only
Add expander (4HP right side) — places the PS-X expander against the right edge of this module
